# What is it you'd say you, uh, do here- exactly?

This is probably my `favorite` question when family or friends ask me what I do. What is my job. I started out in marketing, where my job was nebulous. One day I was a community manager who fielded feedback and turned that into actionable suggestions. The next I was a blogger, who did whatever a blogger does. I still don't know myself. The question of what I did was much harder to answer. 

"I blog." 

"What do you blog about?"

"I write articles for companies that talk about their product."

"Who reads these articles?" 

"Decision makers."

"What do they care?"

"The articles lead to sales."

"How?"

"I honestly couldn't tell you."

And on and on it went like that for me. I was making snake oil as far as I was concerned. 

And then I found what I was destined to do after I'd graduated: the field of technical writing. I had to go through tech support to get there, but becoming an expert at things takes steps. But now I can at least give a simple answer to what I do: I write instruction manuals. 

But things began to change when my 80+ year old in-law hit me with: "Can't AI do that yet?"

And I had to concede that yes it could. And he said something I wasn't prepared for: "so what do you do, then?"

It's a fair question and not one I could easily answer then. 

I am a senior technical writer for a mid-size and I've got multiple AI agents working under me handling everything from publishing to code check. I spend maybe 10-20% of my day "writing" and the rest is spent architecting, navigating, and ideating. Sometimes ideating happens after work when I'm walking my dogs or out and about. I'll see things that will jar me into taking action next time I am at my desk. 

I really have become a "senior", with AI as my junior. I miss people, though. But AI follows the style guide 100% of the time. It formats things according to what I'm looking for. It surfaces key details and yes, some of them are wrong, but they are getting fewer and farther between. What worries me now are the things I am not seeing.

And now I'm on a quest: automate myself out of a job. 

That's what I do. I automate until they lay me off. And I use that spare time to write this shit.
